prompt.1: After this summer's big fire near Summerland, what should the province do first about wildfires?
prompt.2: After the Bald Range fire emptied Summerland and part of Peachland, where should the province put its wildfire effort first?
prompt.3: After the Bald Range fire near Summerland, where should the province put its main wildfire money and effort before next summer?
prompt.4: The Bald Range fire emptied Summerland and part of Peachland in August 2026 and destroyed about 150 structures. What comes first?
prompt.5: The Bald Range fire (August 7 to 28, 2026, about 25,000 hectares) emptied Summerland and part of Peachland, killed one person and destroyed about 150 structures. Which wildfire approach should the province take first?

context.1: A huge fire near Summerland this summer forced thousands of people from their homes and destroyed many houses. The province fights fires, pays for prevention work around towns, and helps people rebuild. Parties disagree on what to spend the next money on.
context.2: The Bald Range fire started near Summerland on August 7. About 20,000 people were ordered out of Summerland and Peachland, one person died, and about 150 buildings were damaged or destroyed, many of them uninsured. Earlier this year the province's community fire-prevention grants ran out of money. Parties disagree on what to fund first.
context.3: The Bald Range fire began northwest of Summerland on August 7, 2026; all of Summerland and part of Peachland were evacuated, one woman died and about 150 structures were lost before it was held on August 28. In January the FireSmart community grant program closed its intake for lack of money; the 2026 budget later added $15 million. The NDP offers rebuilding help, the Conservatives aircraft, CentreBC guaranteed grants, the Greens long-term restoration funding. OneBC has no position.
context.4: The Bald Range fire (August 7 to 28, 2026) burned about 25,000 hectares northwest of Summerland; a provincial state of emergency on August 8 ordered about 20,000 residents of Summerland and Peachland out, one 80-year-old woman died, and about 150 structures were damaged or destroyed, many uninsured. The FireSmart Community Funding program closed its 2026 intake on January 30 for lack of funds; Budget 2026 then added $15 million and the 2027 intake opened October 1. Fire management was budgeted at $235.7 million for 2026/27 with spending forecast at $850 million by September. Prevention, aircraft, grants and recovery compete for the next dollar.
context.5: The Bald Range fire started August 7, 2026 about 15 km northwest of Summerland; a provincial state of emergency followed on August 8 with evacuation orders for about 20,000 people in Summerland and the Peachland area. One 80-year-old woman died while evacuating, about 150 structures were damaged or destroyed, and the fire was held on August 28 at about 25,000 hectares. Many owners were uninsured or underinsured. The Union of BC Municipalities reported in January 2026 that the FireSmart Community Funding intake closed on January 30 for lack of funds; Budget 2026 added $15 million for core FireSmart. Fire management: $235.7 million voted for 2026/27, $850 million forecast as of September 14. On October 2 the Conservatives released a wildfire plan in the Okanagan and Eby announced recovery support in Summerland.

prompt.1: Kelowna wants forced care for the sickest drug users. What should the province do?
prompt.2: Kelowna's council wants a regional forced-treatment facility and its downtown drug-use site closed. What should the province do?
prompt.3: Kelowna's council wants a regional involuntary care facility and its downtown consumption site closed. What should be done?
prompt.4: Kelowna asked for a regional involuntary care facility and for Health Canada not to renew its consumption site. What now?
prompt.5: Kelowna council asked Health Canada not to renew the Outreach Urban Health consumption site (3,466 RCMP calls since 2021) and asked the province for a regional mandatory care facility. Which provincial approach?

context.1: Kelowna's downtown has people living on the street with addiction and mental illness. The city wants a regional centre where the sickest can be made to get care, and wants a downtown supervised drug-use site closed. Parties disagree on what the province should pay for.
context.2: In September Kelowna's council asked Ottawa not to renew a downtown site where people use drugs under supervision, citing thousands of police calls. It also asked the province for a regional facility where the sickest people could be treated against their will. The province decides where such facilities go and how police and hospitals are funded. Parties differ widely.
context.3: On September 1 Kelowna council asked Health Canada not to renew the downtown supervised consumption site in 2027, citing 3,466 police calls since 2021, and repeated its request to the province for a regional mandatory care facility. Eby said on October 2 he is looking for a site that can open at once; the Conservatives would expand police powers; CentreBC would fund downtown safety teams; the Greens would expand supervised sites; OneBC would close them.
context.4: Kelowna council's September 1 letter asked Health Canada to deny the 2027 renewal of the Pandosy Street supervised consumption site, citing 3,466 RCMP calls since 2021, and repeated its request to the province for 'a regional mandatory care facility within the Okanagan'. The province's involuntary care beds are in Surrey and Maple Ridge, none in the Okanagan. Site licences are federal; the provincial decisions are where a regional facility goes, Mental Health Act changes, and health and policing funding. Eby said in Kelowna on October 2 the province is seeking a site 'that can be used immediately', with staffing the limit.
context.5: Kelowna council's September 1, 2026 letter asked Health Canada to deny the 2027 renewal of the Outreach Urban Health supervised consumption site, citing 3,466 RCMP calls since it opened in 2021, and repeated the request for a regional mandatory care facility in the Okanagan; Okanagan mayors have asked that the Oliver Correctional Centre be used to capacity. The BC Coroners Service reported 132 toxic drug deaths in Interior Health in 2026 to June, 70 of them in the Okanagan. The federal decriminalization exemption expired January 31, 2026. Involuntary care beds opened at Surrey Pretrial (10, April 2025) and Alouette Homes in Maple Ridge (18, June 2025); none are in the Okanagan. On October 2 Eby said sites have been identified that could be used immediately, staffing permitting, and that consumption sites 'save lives' if well run.

prompt.1: Kelowna's new care home is on hold and Vernon's was cancelled. What should the province do?
prompt.2: The province paused Kelowna's new care home in February, and a private 250-bed Vernon project was cancelled in October. What now?
prompt.3: Budget 2026 paused seven care home builds including Kelowna's, and a private 250-bed Vernon project was pulled. What now?
prompt.4: Budget 2026 paused seven care builds at up to $1.8 million a bed, and a private 250-bed Vernon project was cancelled. What now?
prompt.5: Budget 2026 (February 17) paused seven long-term care projects (Kelowna, Abbotsford, Campbell River, Chilliwack, Delta, Fort St. John, Squamish; about $1.4 billion); Park Place pulled its 250-bed Vernon project on October 7. Which approach?

context.1: Many Okanagan seniors wait for a place in a care home. The province put a new Kelowna care home on hold, and a company gave up on a big Vernon project over funding worries. Parties disagree on how to build more beds.
context.2: In February 2026 the provincial budget paused seven planned long-term care homes, including the replacement for Cottonwoods in Kelowna. In October a private company cancelled a 250-bed Vernon project, blaming uncertainty about operating costs and funding. Parties disagree on whether to restart the public projects, let funding follow seniors to private providers, or both.
context.3: Budget 2026 paused seven long-term care projects, including the Cottonwoods replacement in Kelowna. On October 7 Park Place Seniors Living pulled its 250-bed Vernon project, citing uncertainty about operating costs and funding; the care providers' association says the government has 'no discernable plan for seniors care'. On October 5 the NDP promised to resume the seven projects. The Conservatives would let funding follow seniors to any qualified provider. CentreBC would restart all seven with a factory-built design.
context.4: Budget 2026 paused seven long-term care projects: Abbotsford, Campbell River, Chilliwack, Delta, Fort St. John, Kelowna (the Cottonwoods replacement) and Squamish, about $1.4 billion to complete, citing costs up to $1.8 million a bed. On October 7 Park Place cancelled its 250-bed Vernon project, citing uncertainty about operating costs and funding; the BC Care Providers Association says 20,000 beds are needed by 2035. The NDP (October 5) would resume the seven with the July 2026 Canada-BC agreement. The Conservatives (October 9) would cut design rules and give waiting seniors portable funding usable at non-government providers. CentreBC would restart all seven with a prefabricated design and bed targets.
context.5: Budget 2026 paused seven long-term care projects: Abbotsford, Campbell River, Chilliwack, Delta, Fort St. John, Kelowna (the Cottonwoods replacement) and Squamish, about $1.4 billion; the province cited per-bed costs up to $1.8 million and a move to a lower-cost uniform design. On October 7, 2026 Park Place confirmed it had pulled a 250-bed Vernon project, citing uncertainty about operating costs and funding; the BC Care Providers Association said the government has 'no discernable plan for seniors care' and 20,000 new beds are needed by 2035. The NDP would resume all seven with July 2026 Canada-BC agreement money (October 5). The Conservatives would cut design rules and give waiting seniors portable public funding usable at non-government providers (October 9). CentreBC would restart all seven with a pre-fabricated design, 2,500 beds under construction by March 2031.
